ricasoli.name: Barone Ricasoli, 2022 harvest (Brolio estate)
ricasoli.note: One estate, not a regional view.

claims.claim: The Consorzio reports no spring frost and no significant hail in Chianti Classico. Jancis Robinson reportedly cites Tuscan spring frost, and individual estates report hail.
Italy's Finest Wines describes a mild winter and dry spring. Bolgheri drought began in late winter and ran through much of summer. Bolgheri had minor spring frost in pockets.
claims.note: Three sources, though frost is one source.

claims.claim: Summer was hot and dry. Ricasoli recorded temperatures over 30 C from May and 38 to 40 C in July, with water stress on stony soils. The Consorzio says heat stayed steady without extreme peaks and spring rain protected the vines.
claims.note: One estate and the Consorzio give different emphases.

claims.claim: Mid-August rain eased the heat in both zones and restarted ripening in Bolgheri. Some Chianti Classico estates saw early July hail.
claims.note: Several sources agree on the rain.

claims.claim: Chianti Classico Sangiovese picking began about 10 September and ran about a month. Ricasoli's Brolio estate picked Sangiovese from 15 September into early October, and Chardonnay from 17 August. Bolgheri harvest began around the third week of August and finished in late September.
claims.note: Consorzio dates for both zones agree with estate and chart data.

claims.claim: Bolgheri yields were low, with small, concentrated berries. For Chianti Classico, the Consorzio gives no volume. Producers say it was above 2021 but below the ten-year average. Ricasoli called it bountiful. Some estates lost up to half their crop.
Chianti Classico: balanced, with good acidity and ripe, soft tannins, enjoyable young. Decanter reportedly gives 4 out of 5 for a variable, near-term annata, and Vinous calls it highly variable.
claims.note: Early Consorzio view is promotional. Decanter and Vinous from search summaries.

claims.claim: Bolgheri: sturdy structure and ripe but grippy tannins, with dark fruit, moderate alcohol and good freshness. Some sources say it may age for decades.
claims.note: Wine Scholar Guild rating is tentative.

claims.claim: Late-ripening Cabernet Sauvignon in Bolgheri lost crop to August rain and September flash floods, according to one account.

conflicts: Frost: the Consorzio says none in Chianti Classico, but Jancis Robinson reportedly cites April frost reducing Tuscan yields. Wine Scholar Guild notes minor spring frost in Bolgheri pockets.

Yields: Consorzio-linked and producer voices say healthy and bountiful, while Robinson and Italy's Finest Wines say low or limited. One estate reportedly lost almost 50% and another lost single-vineyard crus to hail.
gaps: No Chianti Classico hectolitre total for 2022.
Florence hills and Valdarno not covered separately.
Decanter, Vinous and Robinson 2022 pages not read in full.

sheet.vintage: 2022 was hot and very dry, but mid-August rain helped. Picking started early and the wines are ripe and balanced, though yields and quality vary by site.
